content.title: About
content.content: Tortellini are small ring‑shaped pasta filled with a seasoned meat blend of beef, pork, or a mix of both. They are served in a fragrant tomato sauce made from ripe tomatoes, onion, garlic and basil. The dish offers a tender bite, juicy filling and a mildly sweet‑tangy sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortellini originate from Italy and their shape resembles tiny “ears” or “dumplings”.
Traditionally they are hand‑rolled, but modern production often uses specialized molding machines.
Meat fillings can also include veal, turkey or even shrimp besides the classic beef‑pork mix.
Tomato sauce for tortellini is frequently enriched with red wine, adding depth to the flavor.
In Italy tortellini are often served in broth, but with tomato sauce they have become popular worldwide.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat filling provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tortellini contain vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in the sauce
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The pasta provides slow‑releasing carbs that help maintain satiety.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauces often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional tortellini made with wheat flour are unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat fillings can be high in saturated fat; choosing leaner meat reduces this risk.

items.title: Acidity of tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes may trigger heartburn in individuals with high stomach acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tortellini hot, topped with tomato sauce. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan, add fresh basil or a drizzle of olive oil. They pair well with a light arugula salad and a glass of dry red wine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Dry tortellini should be kept in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 12 months. Fresh (frozen) tortellini can be stored in the freezer for up to 3 months. Cooked leftovers cool to room temperature, then refrigerate and consume within 2 days.
